title: From the ERP's CSV to Avro
prompt: The ERP exports accounts as a semicolon-separated CSV with a header line, and the event platform wants Avro. Write `convert(csv_path, avro_path)` so it reads the CSV with the right types and saves it as Avro. `solve` is written for you.
rules: The CSV uses `;` between values and has a header line. Values that contain `;` are in double quotes.
Columns keep the types they have in `accounts`: `credit_limit` is `decimal(12,2)`, `created_on` a date and `is_active` a boolean.
The Avro folder may exist from the night before: replace it.
`solve` returns what reading the Avro folder gives: every account, the columns of `accounts` in order. An empty export gives an empty result.
hints: `spark.read.csv(path, sep=..., header=True, schema=...)` reads the file. Without a schema every column is text.
Write the schema as a string, one `name TYPE` per column, in the file's column order. Money is `DECIMAL(12,2)`.
Avro keeps the types you read, so `write.mode("overwrite").format("avro").save(avro_path)` is all the writing needs.
explanation: Read with `spark.read.csv(csv_path, sep=";", header=True, schema="account_id STRING, ..., credit_limit DECIMAL(12,2), created_on DATE, is_active BOOLEAN")` and save with `.write.mode("overwrite").format("avro").save(avro_path)`. CSV is plain text, so the types have to come from your schema; Avro then stores them with the data. `inferSchema=True` guesses `double` for the credit limit, the default comma separator puts each whole line in the first column, and forgetting `header=True` reads the header line as an account.
